President Donald Trump’s recent approval rating also provides another indication of the current political environment ahead of the 2026 midterms.

Data from the October 23-26 Economist/YouGov poll shows that 39% of registered voters approve of President Trump's job performance and 58% disapprove, a net approval rating of -19 percentage points. Historically, the party of the sitting president has struggled during midterm elections, especially if presidential approval ratings are low.

## Trump remains underwater in national polling averages

Trump’s new low in the Economist/YouGov poll comes as several national polling averages show substantially more Americans disapproving than approving of his job performance.

As of Thursday, Nov. 12, the RealClearPolitics average put Trump at 38.7% approval and 59.1% disapproval. [...] A majority also said Trump is using the presidency for personal gain, while 50% said they support Congress blocking his White House ballroom.

Trump's latest bad numbers come days after he saw his lowest approval rating in Economist/YouGov polling since September.

The poll, released Saturday, Nov. 7, showed Trump's approval rating at 36%, down three percentage points from the previous Economist/YouGov survey on Oct. 29, days before the Nov. 3 Election Day.

Trump's near-career low in the newest Reuters/Ipsos poll comes as national polling averages continue to show his approval sinking deeper and deeper underwater.
